instruction: Look at two_sided_housing.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. Create two independent Coordinate Systems or setups for two_sided_housing.step. Side A machines the pocket and four holes; side B machines the two counterbores. The two setup Z axes must point in opposite directions. Do not force exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, or internal tool-library IDs if SOLIDWORKS CAM's Technology Database assigns stable defaults; use suitable installed tool-library entries for the required operation types and let the posted NC program reflect those real CAM selections. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-20_sideA.nc, C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-20_sideB.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For milling tasks, prefer m3axis-tutorial.ctl, mach_iii.ctl, or haas_vf3.ctl; for turning tasks, use an installed turning .ctl post such as fanuc_t2axis.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s).
source: SOLIDWORKS CAM product overview: https://www.solidworks.com/product/solidworks-cam ; SOLIDWORKS 2025 CAM What's New: https://help.solidworks.com/2025/english/WhatsNew/c_wn_cam.htm ; CAMWorks 2.5 Axis Milling: https://camworks.com/modules/25axis-milling/ ; CAMWorks Universal Post Generator: https://camworks.com/universal-post-generator/
